guide:
## Overview

[Fish Audio Drama 3](https://huggingface.co/fishaudio/drama-3) is a
text-to-speech model built for multi-character scenes and long-form content:
a 35B-total / 3B-active MoE text backbone plus a codebook decoder that
produces 10 codebooks per frame, decoded to **44.1 kHz mono** audio. It
supports zero-shot voice cloning, speaker tags (`<|speaker:0|>` …
`<|speaker:15|>`) and inline event tags such as `[sighs]` or `[laughs]`.

vLLM-Omni serves it as two stages on one GPU: the AR stage (backbone +
codebook decoder) streams frames to the codec stage, which returns audio
through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` API.

## Prerequisites

- **Hardware**: a single CUDA GPU with at least 48 GB. Reference run:
  1x H100 80 GB (stage-0 weights 36.9 GiB).
- **vLLM-Omni** with Drama 3 support, on vLLM >= 0.31.

## Installation

```bash
uv venv && source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install vllm==0.31.0 --torch-backend=auto
uv pip install git+https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni.git
```

## Launch the server

The deploy config (`vllm_omni/deploy/fish_omni.yaml`) is picked up
automatically from `model_type=fish_omni`:

```bash
vllm serve fishaudio/drama-3 --omni --port 8000
```

The first request after start compiles kernels and takes about 10 s;
send a few warmup requests before measuring latency.

## Client usage

### Voice cloning (reference audio + transcript)

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/speech \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "fishaudio/drama-3",
    "input": "The quarterly report is due on Thursday, so please finish it by noon.",
    "voice": "default",
    "ref_audio": "https://huggingface.co/datasets/zhaochenyang20/seed-tts-eval-mini/resolve/main/en/prompt-wavs/common_voice_en_10119832.wav",
    "ref_text": "We asked over twenty different people, and they all said it was his.",
    "response_format": "wav"
  }' --output cloned.wav
```

### Streaming

Add `"stream": true, "response_format": "pcm"` to receive Server-Sent
Events whose `speech.audio.delta` events carry base64 16-bit PCM at 44.1 kHz.

### Event and emotion tags

Non-verbal events and delivery are controlled only through the input text.
Write a short natural-language descriptor in square brackets where the event
should happen:

```text
[sighs] Fine. If we miss it, it's on you. [laughs] Well, maybe that's fair.
```

- There is no fixed tag list. Tags are ordinary text (no special tokens), so
  any short descriptor is accepted; wordings close to the ones Fish Audio
  documents work best: `[sighs]`, `[laughs]`, `[laughing]`, `[whisper]`,
  `[angry]`, `[excited]`, `[pause]`.
- Speaker tags `<|speaker:0|>` … `<|speaker:15|>` are the only special control
  tokens: `"<|speaker:0|> Hi. <|speaker:1|> Hello."`. Text without a leading
  speaker tag is spoken by speaker 0.
- The reference clip also shapes delivery implicitly (an expressive or
  pause-heavy reference carries over), but it is not a targeted control.
- A tag or filler word at the very start of a line (`[sighs] …`, `Yeah. …`)
  more often renders the first word or event and then only silence until
  `max_new_tokens`; mid-sentence tags are more reliable.

## Performance

1x H100 80 GB, both stages on one GPU, streaming `/v1/audio/speech`, one
voice-clone reference, temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.9 / top_k 30, warm server:

| Concurrency | First audio (p50) | RTF |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 126 ms | 0.28 |
| 4 | 246 ms | 0.40 |
| 8 | 360 ms | 0.51 |

Voice cloning, 5 public Common Voice reference voices x 4 English
sentences: Whisper-large-v3 WER 0.000.

## Known limitations

- Output is **44.1 kHz mono**; voice cloning requires **both** `ref_audio`
  and `ref_text`.
- Some takes finish speaking and then keep emitting silence until
  `max_new_tokens`, most often on prompts that start with fillers or event
  tags; cap `max_new_tokens` to the expected length of the text.
- Editing as continuation (`previous_takes`) and long-text chunking are not
  exposed through the speech API yet.

## References

- [Model card](https://huggingface.co/fishaudio/drama-3)
- vLLM-Omni support: vllm-project/vllm-omni [#8900](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/8900)
